title.narrative: Fiscal strategy

description.narrative: Fiscal strategy

comment.narrative: The Pakistan government is currently engaged with the IMF trying to agree on a path which would be compatible with fiscal sustainability in the medium and longer term. The PFMII project has engaged systematically at the ministerial level providing technical advice on the options for improving the fiscal situation including coping with the need for subsidy reduction in the energy sector. These analyses are feeding into the ongoing negotiations with the IMF.Substantial support at federal and provincial level through the design and support for Medium Term Fiscal Framework MTFF and Budget Strategy Paper BSP in all three areas Federal Sindh and Balochistan. Extensive support to Federal Government on key fiscal topics including subsidy policy through the former Subsidy Unit on the MoF and in the context of engagement of MoF with the IMF.As agreement has now been reached with the IMF in relation to the ongoing programme it is now appropriate to indicate a higher level of achievementAn important area of work in the fourth year of the project has been the support for the development of pensions policy as a contribution to supporting longer term budget sustainability. This has led to the finalisation of legal instruments for pension reform in the federal Government and the finalization of a draft law on the establishment of a retirement fund by the Federal Government.The project has supported the development of a mediumterm fiscal strategy to be presented to the incoming minister of finance following the February 2024 elections.The project has exceeded the target for this outcome

title.narrative: Information on commitment ceilings

description.narrative: Information on commitment ceilings

comment.narrative: Commitment reform process defined but not yet implemented. In the Federal Government the project has worked with the Budget Wing in the MoF to prepare the plan for the progressive implementation of commitment control. However successful implementation of commitment controls will take several years as it will require activation of and training in the modules of the government financial management IT system relating to such control. Progress in Sindh has started with familiarization of the key officials with the key steps required to implement commitment control. Balochistan province does not currently have the absorption capacity to be able to implement commitment control in the short to medium term.

comment.narrative: Important contribution through i indepth analysis of the weaknesses in public investment at federal level ii drafting of section on planning and investment in the federal PFM Act of 2019. This includes strengthened requirements for quality control on the process of technical analysis and approval of projects prior to their inclusion in the budget. In Sindh and Balochistan provinces the project has supported the development of comprehensive Planning and Investment Manuals through a lengthy consultative process working with teams in the respective Planning and Development Departments PDD The Sindh manual has been officially adopted and the Balochistan manual is currently at te stage of awaiting official approval. This will lead to comprehensive training of officers across the provincial governments in the application of the manual which incorporates stronger measures and procedures to establish and maintain quality control on the selection and implementation of capital projects through the budget.The project has exceeded the target set for this outcome
